name: Posterior meniscofemoral lig. (Wrisberg)
description: Posterior meniscofemoral ligament: an inconstant band from the lateral meniscus posterior horn, behind the PCL, to a fan-shaped attachment on the medial femoral condyle. An oblique low-signal band behind the PCL on posterior coronal images and a small dot behind it on sagittal.
variants_pitfalls: Present in about 70% of knees and the one more often seen on MRI; at least one meniscofemoral ligament is present in about 91–93% of cadaver knees.

Pseudotear at its insertion in 39–63% of knees, usually an oblique line. The attachment normally reaches about three 3 mm images lateral to the PCL; 4 or more, especially with an ACL tear, raises the possibility of a real tear.
Wrisberg rip: with an ACL tear a vertical tear can run along the attachment; unlike the pseudotear it extends further lateral.
On one sagittal image it can pass for a loose body or fragment; follow it on coronal images to the condyle. On MRI it often seems to end on the PCL.
Wrisberg-variant discoid: with no posterior meniscotibial attachment the posterior horn is hypermobile, and MRI may look normal unless locked.
